name: Overtime Paycheck Garnishment Check
outcome: Verify an overtime paycheck's garnishment withholding in four recompute stages: first compute the FLSA regular rate and overtime premium per 29 CFR 778, Subpart C, including nondiscretionary-bonus reallocation (ART-340), then compute federal income tax withholding by the IRS Publication 15-T percentage method for the declared tax year edition (ART-338), then compute gross-to-net pay with FICA at that year's Social Security wage base (ART-339), then recompute how much of the employee's disposable earnings each order in a caller-declared garnishment stack may lawfully withhold under the CCPA Title III caps, compared against a garnishment notice where one is supplied (ART-572), closing with a session receipt aggregating the run's execution hashes (CRY-05). Disposable earnings for the art-572 run are gross earnings minus legally-required deductions, using the gross and legally-required-deduction figures cited from the art-339 run; net pay is never an input to the art-572 run. The aggregate ceiling in the art-572 run, equal to the single highest individual cap present in the stack, is a documented simplification in that run's not_proven list. Wage, filing, deduction, and order figures are caller-supplied inputs; each stage is an independent recompute from its own declared inputs. A mismatch is an arithmetic finding, never a legal determination about an order's validity. Not legal advice and not tax advice.
